overview: Three index sheets (1940-41) summarize Japanese press controls: cuts to foreign correspondents' cables, scarce independent commentary, suppressed Axis-negotiation reporting, a news-publication control law, hostile anti-Roosevelt press treatment, and a ban on foreign missions' public bulletins.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: Author or sender of reports from the U.S. mission in Japan

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: State Department official identified with PA/H

people.role: Major and source of information about censorship of news leaving Japan

people.role: Editor of the Japan Times and Advertiser

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Grew report on censorship of foreign correspondents
subfiles.about: An index entry summarizes Grew’s January 15, 1940 report on the widening disparity between domestic press freedom and censorship of foreign correspondents’ outgoing dispatches.
subfiles.summary: Grew's Telegram 21 reports domestic press growing unrestrained while foreign dispatches were drastically cut, warning American coverage might become inadequate.

subfiles.title: List of Papers, sheet 5: Japanese censorship measures in 1940
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes four 1940 records concerning institutional censorship, press bans, restrictions on foreign reporting, and surveillance of liberal expression.
subfiles.summary: Sheet 5: a Cabinet Intelligence Bureau's censorship, Axis-negotiation press bans, Hornbeck's near-total news blackout note, and Grew's surveillance despatch.

subfiles.title: List of Papers, page 6: News control and anti-Roosevelt publicity in 1941
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes four 1941 records on Japan’s news-control law, disparaging coverage of Roosevelt, and restrictions on foreign missions’ publications.
subfiles.summary: Page 6: Law No. 37 on news control, anti-Roosevelt commentary, a Japan Times cartoon, and a foreign-mission bulletin ban.

interest: Shows escalating 1940-41 Japanese press censorship, including cable cuts, anti-Roosevelt publicity, and foreign-mission bulletin bans.
